scenario.title: 餐點有問題，禮貌地反映
scenario.context: 在國外餐廳遇到問題，直接說 This is wrong 容易讓氣氛變僵。英文客訴的關鍵是「軟化」：用 There seems to be… / It seems to be… 把問題說成觀察，而不是指責，服務生也更願意幫你處理。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Excuse me, I'm sorry, but there seems to be a mistake. I ordered the steak medium, and this seems to be well-done.
lines.zh: 不好意思，抱歉，好像有點問題。我點的牛排是五分熟，這個看起來是全熟。

lines.speaker: Server
lines.en: Oh, I'm so sorry about that. I'll have the kitchen make you a new one right away.
lines.zh: 啊，真的很抱歉。我馬上請廚房重做一份。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Thank you. Also, we've been waiting for our drinks for a while. They seem to have been forgotten.
lines.zh: 謝謝。另外，我們的飲料等了一陣子了，好像被忘記了。

lines.speaker: Server
lines.en: You're right, I apologize. The drinks are on the house tonight.
lines.zh: 您說得對，很抱歉。今晚的飲料由我們招待。

lines.speaker: Server
lines.en: Here's your steak. Medium this time, I promise.
lines.zh: 您的牛排，這次是五分熟，我保證。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Perfect. Oh, this really hits the spot.
lines.zh: 完美。喔，這真的太對味了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: How was that place near the harbor?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: The service wasn't up to par at first, but they fixed everything.
lines.zh: 一開始服務不太到位，但他們都處理好了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Better than the one we went to last year. That was such a tourist trap.
lines.zh: 比我們去年去的那間好。那間根本是觀光客陷阱。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Ugh, don't remind me. The seafood didn't seem to be fresh at all.
lines.zh: 唉，別提了。海鮮看起來一點都不新鮮。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: And it cost twice as much as everywhere else.
lines.zh: 而且價錢是別家的兩倍。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Lesson learned: always check the reviews first.
lines.zh: 學到教訓：一定要先看評價。

patterns.en: Excuse me, I'm sorry to bother you, but ___.
There seems to be a mistake with my order.
patterns.zh: 我的餐點好像有點問題。

patterns.en: This isn't quite what I ordered.
I think this might be undercooked.
We've been waiting for quite a while.
Could we speak to the manager, please?
patterns.zh: 我們可以跟經理談談嗎？
patterns.note: 最後手段，語氣要保持平靜

patterns.en: I'd appreciate it if you could ___.
patterns.zh: 如果你能 ___ 我會很感激。

chinglish.right: I think there's been a mix-up with my order.
chinglish.why: 直接說 wrong 帶指責。英文客訴習慣把問題說成「好像有誤會」，讓對方有台階下。

chinglish.wrong: This steak is not cooked enough, change one for me.
chinglish.right: This steak seems a bit undercooked. Could I get it cooked a little longer?
chinglish.why: change one for me 是中式直翻，而且語氣像命令。

chinglish.right: Could I speak to the manager, please?
chinglish.why: 中文「叫你們經理出來」直翻很兇。

chinglish.wrong: It seems like is not fresh.
chinglish.right: It doesn't seem to be fresh. / It seems like it's not fresh.
chinglish.why: seems like 後面要接完整子句（有主詞）。

grammar.title: There seems to be… / seem to V
grammar.oneLiner: seem 把肯定的陳述變成「看起來像」的觀察，是客訴、提意見時最好用的軟化工具。
whenToUse: There seems to be + 名詞：There seems to be a problem.（比 There is a problem 委婉）
主詞 + seem(s) to + 原形：The steak seems to be well-done.
seem to have + p.p.（過去的推測）：They seem to have forgotten our drinks.
seem + 形容詞：It seems a bit cold.
It seems like / It seems that + 子句：It seems like there's been a mistake.
否定：doesn't seem to…：It doesn't seem to be working.
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文客訴時常直接說事實：「這個沒熟」「你們送錯了」，語氣靠聲調調整。英文則靠句型軟化，seem 就是其中最常用的一個。台灣人會用 seem 但常把結構弄錯，例如 It seems like is cold（少了主詞），或 There seem is a problem。

examples.correct: There seems to be a problem with the bill.
examples.incorrect: There seem is a problem with the bill.
examples.note: There seems to be + 名詞。

examples.correct: This dish seems to be missing the sauce.
examples.note: 主詞 + seems to + 原形。

examples.correct: They seem to have forgotten our order.
examples.note: seem to have + p.p.：推測過去。

examples.correct: It seems like the kitchen is really busy.
examples.incorrect: It seems like is really busy.
examples.note: seems like 後接完整子句。

examples.correct: The soup doesn't seem to be very hot.

quiz.question: ___ to be a mistake on our bill.
quiz.explanation: There seems to be + 名詞。

quiz.question: The waiter seems ___ have forgotten our drinks.
Which complaint sounds the most polite?
options: You gave me the wrong dish.
I think there seems to be a mix-up with my order.
quiz.explanation: 用 seem 軟化最禮貌。

slang.usage: It's on the house. = 這是店家請的。

examples.en: Dessert is on the house tonight.
The owner said our second round was on the house.

slang.meaning: （食物飲料）正是我想要的、很對味
slang.usage: 剛好滿足需求時說：That really hit the spot.

examples.en: A cold beer after a long hike really hits the spot.
examples.zh: 健行完來瓶冰啤酒，太爽了。

examples.en: That noodle soup hit the spot on a rainy day.
examples.zh: 下雨天那碗湯麵真是太對味了。

slang.usage: par 源自高爾夫的「標準桿」。也可以說身體狀況 I'm not feeling up to par.

risk.note: 委婉的批評，職場也可以用。

examples.en: The food wasn't up to par tonight. Maybe the chef was off.
examples.zh: 今晚的菜不如平常，也許主廚休假。

examples.en: His work hasn't been up to par lately.
examples.zh: 他最近的工作表現不如以往。

slang.meaning: 觀光客陷阱（又貴又普通的地方）
slang.usage: 專門賺觀光客錢、品質不怎麼樣的店或景點。

examples.en: Avoid the restaurants right next to the temple. They're tourist traps.
examples.zh: 避開廟旁邊的餐廳，那都是觀光客陷阱。

examples.en: It's a bit of a tourist trap, but the view is worth it.
examples.zh: 有點坑觀光客，但景色值得。

review.question: Our table ___ yet.
review.explanation: 複習第 42 單元：現在完成被動。

review.question: Could you fill ___ this form, please?
review.explanation: 複習第 41 單元：fill out / fill in。

review.question: If the food ___ cold, send it back.
review.explanation: 複習第 39 單元：if 子句用現在式。

review.question: You waited an hour for your food? That ___ have been annoying.
review.explanation: 複習第 35 單元：must 推測。

review.question: Could you tell me ___?
review.explanation: 複習第 27 單元：間接問句用肯定語序。

review.question: There ___ to be a problem with my order.
